statement: The system shall turn satellite observations into usable products quickly and reliably for NOAA operational users, climate users, and other civilian customers.
The system shall provide product continuity during failures.
The system shall preserve selected data in the long-term archive.
Success shall be measured by how well the system delivers the right products to the right users on time.
Success shall be measured by acceptable data quality and availability.
Success shall be measured by minimal disruption when parts of the system fail.
The system shall support electronic distribution to authorized customers using whatever operational channel NOAA selects.
The system shall deliver selected products into the archive interface or transfer path used by the archive system for long-term archive delivery.
The system shall not treat archive delivery as a customer delivery.
For archive deliveries, the system shall prioritize completeness, integrity, and timeliness over a specific user-facing format.
The system shall support a secure network-based service for product ordering and retrieval for authorized users.
The system shall support automated delivery for customers who subscribe to routine products.
The system shall support push delivery for recurring operational feeds.
Some products shall be restricted to certain user classes or distribution agreements.
The entitlement matrix should be driven by product sensitivity.
The system shall continue service as much as possible when a primary product delivery channel is unavailable.
For important operational products, the system shall alert operators immediately when delivery cannot proceed on the primary channel.
There is not yet a hard rule defining which customer classes receive automatic failover versus manual handling.
Fallback behavior shall preserve continuity with traceability.
The system shall focus on how it ingests satellite data.
The system shall generate and distribute products.
The system shall support customer access and order tracking.
The system shall remain reliable through outages and archive delivery.
The system shall ingest source data feeds.
The system shall provide manual support when something goes wrong.
The system shall receive observations.
The system shall provide better customer self-service for registration.
The system shall provide stronger monitoring to detect integrity problems.
The system shall send selected products to the long-term archive without extra handling.
The system shall provide the listed main capabilities as one operational service rather than as separate tools.
The system shall provide clearer audit trails for what was produced and delivered.
The system shall support role-based access so that only authorized users can see or order certain products.
The system shall take the satellite observation stream from the polar-orbiting platforms and turn it into usable operational and climate products for NOAA and other civilian users.
The system shall ingest source data reliably.
The system shall deliver products quickly and consistently to the right users.
The system shall automate the end-to-end flow.
The system shall support ordering and customer access.
The system shall provide product status and assistance.
The system shall preserve critical products in the long-term archive.
The system shall remain dependable during outages so that product delivery and internal operations can continue with minimal disruption.
The system shall maintain product quality and integrity.
The system shall ensure availability of core processing and distribution services during failures or recover quickly after failures.
When such issues occur, the workaround is usually manual coordination with the operations teams.
When such issues occur, the workaround can include rerunning the processing chain.
The system shall support operations staff who monitor ingestion, processing, distribution, and continuity.
The system shall support product specialists who respond to quality questions and provide customer support.
The system shall provide selected products to NOAA program and archive stakeholders for long-term preservation and oversight.
The system shall support authorized civilian and operational customers who order products.
The system shall support authorized civilian and operational customers who check order status.
The operations or ground system team shall handle data ingestion.
The processing team shall run product generation.
Quality assurance shall be shared between automated checks in the system and product specialists.
A help desk or product services group shall handle customer support.
The system shall support graceful failover or restart capability so it can pick up where it left off.
The system shall handle automated reruns.
The system shall route selected outputs to the archive.
The system shall provide help when something is missing or incorrect.
The dashboard shall show the current state of each data feed, processing step, product queue, and distribution channel in one place.
The dashboard shall provide clear indicators for whether each item is healthy, delayed, or failed.
The system shall manage status or audit records that track what happened at each step.
Status records shall indicate whether each feed, product, and order is pending, in process, complete, or failed.
The system shall create a support case for a help request.
The registration record shall identify the customer and the customer’s allowed access.
Orders or subscriptions shall be associated with the registration record.
Each order shall reference the specific product set or service the customer wants.
Status records shall track the lifecycle of requests and any deliveries tied to them.
Product access shall use the relationships among records to control what gets delivered and to help support staff view the customer, the order, the current state, and past issues in one trail.
Only registered and authorized customers shall be allowed to place orders or receive products.
The system shall respect product priority and delivery schedules when processing orders and products.
During normal operations, the system shall allow routine deliveries and standard orders to flow automatically.
During an outage or processing failure, the system shall preserve the queue.
During an outage or processing failure, the system shall capture the failure status.
During an outage or processing failure, the system shall recover in priority order so that time-sensitive products are handled first.
Customer support staff shall be able to immediately see whether an issue is a permissions problem, a processing delay, or a system outage.
Customer support workflows shall support advising the customer, manually intervening, or waiting for automated recovery.
The system shall comply with applicable NOAA and federal IT controls related to security.
The system shall comply with applicable NOAA and federal IT controls related to access control.
The system shall comply with applicable NOAA and federal IT controls related to auditability.
The system shall fit into NOAA's approved hosting and network environment.
The system shall satisfy record retention and archival obligations for selected products and status records.
The system shall use encryption where required by NOAA policy.
The system shall be able to verify that delivered and archived outputs have not been altered.
Order placement may take longer when entitlement validation or delivery queuing is required.
The system should confirm order placement quickly enough that the user knows the request was accepted.
The system shall scale to growing data volumes by adding processing and storage capacity without redesigning the entire workflow.
The system shall allow ingestion functions to operate in a queued or distributed manner.
The system shall allow product generation functions to operate in a queued or distributed manner.
The system shall allow delivery functions to operate in a queued or distributed manner.
The system shall allow archive functions to operate in a queued or distributed manner.
The system shall ensure that one busy area does not stall other functions.
The system shall provide enough headroom and monitoring to spot bottlenecks early.
The system design shall support traceable workflows.
The system shall support controlled operational procedures for review, retention, and disposal.
The system shall use controlled workflow steps for registration, ordering, delivery, and archival.
The system shall define handling for exceptions such as failed deliveries or suspected unauthorized access.
The system shall include approved and tracked retention and disposal steps rather than allowing individual staff to handle them manually.
Customer and order-related records shall not be discarded arbitrarily.
The system shall use a phased cutover instead of a big-bang switch for migration.
The system shall support a period of parallel operation during migration.
The system shall allow users to compare results during the parallel operation period.
The system shall allow gaps to be fixed before the old system is fully retired.
The system shall use predefined translation rules and interface adapters to normalize legacy formats into the new product and metadata standards without changing the source records themselves.
The system should preserve provenance and lineage where possible.
The system should enable users to see what was converted.
The system should enable users to see the assumptions under which data was converted.
The system shall perform validation checks because satellite streams may have different quality levels and metadata completeness.
The system shall use manual review for edge cases before data is made operational.
The system interface shall be status-driven and task-oriented.
The dashboard shall allow a new operator to see what needs attention at a glance without needing to know all internal details.
The dashboard shall provide clear color-coded health indicators.
The dashboard shall provide concise alerts.
The system shall use consistent terminology.
The system shall provide step-by-step workflow screens that help users move from monitoring to action without getting lost.
The system shall provide quick filters for product specialists.
The system shall provide drill-down detail for product specialists.
The system shall display visible context including source, processing stage, and delivery status.
The system shall be verified for accessibility using a mix of automated checks and hands-on testing.
The accessibility verification process shall include keyboard-only testing.
The accessibility verification process shall include screen reader checks.
The accessibility verification process shall include contrast and zoom verification.
The accessibility verification process shall include reviews against Section 508 and WCAG criteria.
Accessibility verification should ideally involve people who actually use assistive technology.
Any accessibility issues found shall be treated as release blockers.
Any accessibility issues found shall be fixed before go-live.
After an accessibility fix is applied, the system shall be re-tested to ensure the correction did not create a new accessibility problem.
Accessibility needs to be part of the normal development workflow.
Accessibility defects shall be logged in the same way as any other issue.
Accessibility defects shall be prioritized based on user impact and compliance risk.
Definition-of-done criteria shall include accessibility checks before a story can be accepted.
Release gates shall prevent shipment of anything with known serious issues unless an approved exception exists.
After go-live, ongoing accessibility compliance shall be supported by regression testing.
After go-live, ongoing accessibility compliance shall be supported by periodic audits.
Accessibility defects shall be tracked and fixed in the maintenance process just like functional bugs.
The system shall turn raw polar satellite observations into trusted data products for NOAA and other authorized users.
The system shall get the right products out quickly, accurately, and reliably.
The system shall provide timely access to products.
The system shall show whether a user's request is being processed.
The system shall provide support when something looks wrong.
The system shall preserve selected data in the long-term archive for future use.
The system shall handle gaps in source data.
The system shall handle delayed arrivals in source data.
The system shall handle occasional degraded input without losing control of the product flow.
Product coverage shall depend on the satellite pass and on what the sensor actually captured.
Products may be incomplete in some cases.
Latency is a real constraint for the operational side.
The system shall provide registration support functions.
The system shall provide continuity during failures.
The system may receive source observations from upstream satellite or mission data providers.
The system shall support secure, controlled exchange of products because some products are restricted to authorized customers.
The system shall provide standard, well-supported interfaces for product delivery and ordering.
The system shall require authentication and access control for product delivery and ordering interfaces.
The system shall support NOAA operational users as a main customer group.
The system shall support climate and research users as a main customer group.
The system shall support other civilian users who are authorized to receive specific products as a main customer group.
The system shall prioritize long-term availability for climate users.
The system shall apply tighter access controls to some products when required by policy, licensing, or sensitivity.
Registration shall not be completely open.
Eligibility to register depends on whether the requester is an authorized customer for the products they want.
Some users may be able to self-register for basic access.
Higher-sensitivity or restricted products require approval and role-based authorization before access is granted.
Emergency or mission-critical access may be expedited.
The system shall generate products normally when the incoming source data meets the expected quality and completeness thresholds for that product.
The system shall hold a product for reprocessing if the source data is incomplete, corrupted, late, or fails validation.
The exact thresholds and correction rules shall be product-specific and provided by the science and operations teams.
Support shall cover help finding products.
Users shall be able to request help through whatever customer service channel the organization sets up.
Issues involving policy decisions shall be routed to a separate operations or security path rather than handled as routine user support.
The ingest process shall accept source data formats received from the satellite mission feed.
The ingest process shall accept standard metadata required to identify the observation time.
The system shall validate that the metadata is complete enough to support product generation.
The system shall reject or hold for review any format that is missing required fields.
Routine support shall handle straightforward issues such as locating an order.
Issues that change access shall be escalated to the appropriate operations or security contact.
If an issue could indicate a broader integrity problem, it shall be escalated immediately rather than handled as a normal help ticket.
If an input is only missing minor metadata or has a recoverable structural issue, it should be corrected and resubmitted after the problem is fixed.

If the question is whether the data itself is scientifically valid, or whether it came from the right source and time window, the input should go to manual review and approval by the operations or science authority.

Anything that is corrupted beyond recovery, from an unauthorized source, or impossible to reconcile with traceability requirements should be permanently discarded and logged so the reason for rejection can be explained.
The system shall provide a clear catalog of the standard NPOESS-derived products intended for broad operational use.
The system shall include NOAA-specific products needed for NOAA missions in the catalog.
The catalog shall be organized by product family.
The catalog shall be organized by sensor or observation type.
The catalog shall be organized by use case.
The catalog shall allow users to quickly determine whether a product is current, archived, or restricted.
The catalog shall be complete enough for users to search for products.
The catalog shall be complete enough for users to request products.
A product shall be considered timely and reliable enough for immediate use when it is delivered within the required latency window.
If a product arrives late, it shall be marked provisional or withheld from operational decision-making until reviewed.
Anything that fails critical validation shall be routed for later use, correction, or manual review instead of being presented as ready.
The release decision for a time-sensitive product should be based on how much a slightly imperfect product would affect an operational user versus how harmful a delay would be.
If the data are basically complete and the issue is minor, the product shall be released immediately with a clear provisional or degraded-quality flag.
If a short delay is likely to fix a known error without missing the decision window, the product shall be held briefly.
If the correction would miss the usefulness window or the product has an unresolved critical defect, the product shall be held back until the next cycle.
Delivered products and order responses shall include enough integrity information for the user to confirm they received the correct content.
The integrity information may include a checksum.
The system shall run integrity checks before release and again during distribution to detect corruption or mismatches early.
If verification fails, the system shall not treat the item as successfully delivered.
If verification fails and the failure appears to be a transport issue, the system shall retry.
If a check cannot be completed, the response shall be marked indeterminate.
If an incomplete product is still usable for some purposes, the system shall label it clearly as partial or provisional.
If missing pieces affect only narrow use cases, the system shall allow the product to be distributed with a cautionary status.
If missing data undermines the product’s validity or could mislead users, the system shall hold the product back until the gaps are filled.
If the failure looks like a transient delivery problem, the system shall retry automatically a limited number of times.
If the same failure repeats or the check suggests corruption, mismatch, or a bad package, the system shall escalate to support and keep the order flagged as unresolved.
If delivery cannot be confirmed at all, the order shall stay in a non-delivered state until someone verifies it or the customer receives a corrected replacement.
The packaging shall plainly state that the item is partial or incomplete.
If the item is safe for limited use, that safety limitation shall be stated explicitly.
The system should include any verification details that are available before a failure.
If none of the verification can be checked, the user should be told to treat the response as not authoritative until recovery and confirmation are complete.
Records shall be eligible for archive transfer only after they have been fully processed, verified, and released as the final accepted version.
Records shall not be eligible for archive transfer while an operational hold is in effect or while there is a customer support issue tied to the records.
The retention period for archived records shall be determined by NOAA policy and any applicable legal or scientific retention requirements.
The system shall keep records locally until the retention window expires and archive transfer has been confirmed successful.
The system shall place an operational hold on a record if there is an unresolved integrity problem.
The system shall place an operational hold on a record if there is a disputed order.
The system shall place an operational hold on a record if there is an incomplete product issue.
The system shall place an operational hold on a record if there is a failed delivery that still needs correction.
The system shall place an operational hold on a record if it is tied to a support case.
The system shall place an operational hold on a record if it is tied to a reprocessing request.
The system shall place an operational hold on a record if it is tied to a known upstream data issue that could affect the final archive copy.
The system shall keep a record on hold if there is any doubt that it is the final authoritative version.
The formal confirmation of an archive transfer success shall be a positive acknowledgement from the archive destination that the record was received and validated, not merely that it was sent.
The system shall store the archive destination's confirmation against the record.
The system shall update any downstream order or support workflow tied to the record so that staff can see the transfer is complete.
If the archive destination cannot provide the required acknowledgement, the system shall not treat the transfer as closed.
The default retention period for a record shall be whatever the formal records schedule specifies.
The retention period for a record shall be extended if there is a litigation hold.
The retention period for a record shall be extended if there is an audit.
The retention period for a record shall be extended if there is a quality investigation.
The retention period for a record shall be extended if there is a reprocessing event tied to the record.
The system shall not shorten the retention period ad hoc.
Any change to the retention period shall come from an approved policy decision.
The system shall support an exception process for held records.
The exception process shall be very tightly controlled.
Only an authorized records or program manager may approve releasing a held record for archive transfer.
Legal or compliance input shall be included when needed before approving release of a held record for archive transfer.
Approval to release a held record for archive transfer shall be logged.
If a hold is due to integrity or legal issues, the system should be very cautious about allowing any override.
A manager shall only release a held record if the hold is not related to an unresolved legal matter or a known integrity defect.
A manager shall only release a held record if the business owner agrees that the record is ready to be archived despite the hold.
If legal, compliance, or records management has reviewed the release, the system shall capture their approval or objection.
The system shall capture the release reason for a held record release.
The system shall capture the date and time of a held record release.
The system shall capture the approver identity for a held record release.
The system shall capture the specific hold being lifted when a held record is released.
The system shall capture any conditions attached to the release of a held record.
If a release is approved, any attached conditions shall be explicit and narrow.
If a release is approved, the system shall support conditions such as archiving now while retaining a copy in source until the audit completes.
If a release is approved, the system shall support conditions such as transferring only the specified product version, not later revisions.
The system shall record separate concurrence or objection from legal when legal reviewed the release.
The system shall record separate concurrence or objection from compliance when compliance reviewed the release.
The system shall record separate concurrence or objection from records management when records management reviewed the release.
If legal, compliance, or records management did not review the release, the system shall record that they were not part of the approval.
The system shall route specialized issues to a support team with the right expertise, including interpreting a scientific product, resolving a failed order, and explaining an anomaly.
The system shall restrict access to products tied to specific missions or customer agreements.
The system shall restrict access to items under legal hold.
The system shall restrict access to items with export limitations.
The system shall restrict access to items with security limitations.
When a user tries to access a restricted entry, the system shall provide only the appropriate next step, such as contacting the support or authorization group.

The system shall escalate a request to the support or authorization team when a user keeps requesting the same restricted item, challenges the restriction, or indicates an operational need that might qualify for an exception.
The system shall escalate a request when it comes from an account that may have the wrong role assignment or when there is a time-sensitive mission impact.
The system shall block access until a person with authority reviews the request.
The system shall preserve the request context so the reviewer can decide quickly.
The system should support customer-group rules in addition to the general restriction types.
The system should support customer-group rules for access that depends on contract terms.
The system should support customer-group rules for access that depends on a named customer account.
The system should support customer-group rules for access that depends on partner status.
The system should support customer-group rules for access that depends on geographic limits.
The system shall allow access only when the user’s account matches the authorized group and the request is within the contract or mission scope.
When the user’s account does not match the authorized group, the system should deny access by default or route the request for authorization review if there is a plausible business case.
The system should check requests involving region, partner role, or account mismatches against entitlement rules before any product details are exposed.
If a mismatch is clear and there is no existing entitlement or approved exception on record, the system shall stop with a denial.

If the user can point to an active contract, mission exception, or pending approval that might cover the mismatch, the system shall send the request for authorization review instead of ending it outright.
If the rule is ambiguous or the account data appears incomplete, the system shall route the request for authorization review so that a human can confirm the entitlement.
The system shall not reveal partial product content for restricted categories unless a specific business rule allows a safe subset to be shown.
The default behavior shall be no partial disclosure for restricted product categories.
